smm_pool.text: As Buffer has continued to support the individuals, creators, and small and medium businesses who use us, we've had to balance being a relatively small team with making tough decisions. We've had to make one of these recently. After careful deliberation as a team, we've decided to retire Start Page. If you've built a Start Page with us, thank you. Creators, small businesses, and nonprofits have used it as a front door to their work since 2021. Many of our customers were just getting started with their online journey, and a full website can be expensive and fiddly to maintain. Start Page provided a simple, flexible page anyone could build in minutes and share across their social profiles. We don't take ending that lightly, which is why we're giving several months' notice, firm dates, and multiple options to make the transition as hassle-free as possible Here's the timeline: November 4, 2026: We've stopped allowing the creation of new Start Pages November 30, 2026: You'll have tools to move your page somewhere else. February 2, 2027: We'll begin taking down Start Pages that haven't been migrated somewhere else. I'd like to elaborate on why we're doing this, the plan moving forward, and what options we plan to have available. Why we're doing this Having one link that holds everything (also referred to as a link-in-bio tool) is still useful in today's social space. So why are we moving away from it? For us at Buffer, three things have become hard to ignore. We've focused Buffer on our core strengths outside of Start Page. Buffer is a social media toolkit: we help you plan, publish, and learn from your content, and engage with your community across the social channels you use. While Start Page lives in your bio, it sits off to the side of all that. We've wanted to work on Start Page, but it takes away from Buffer's strengths and focus. From a capabilities perspective, Start Page has fallen behind, and catching up would cost us the things you rely on. Link-in-bio and microsite tools have come a long way since 2021, and Start Page hasn't kept pace. Making it best-in-class would mean pulling several teammates away from other key, much-requested improvements to other core Buffer features.
